title: Kumbh Mela: 'Every Four Years'? The Real Gaps Follow Jupiter

beats.say: UNESCO says the Kumbh Mela moves between four Indian cities every four years.
beats.caption: UNESCO: “every four years by rotation”

beats.say: But since twenty thirteen, the gaps ran from one year to five.
beats.caption: Gaps since 2013: 2 · 1 · 5 · 4 years

beats.say: Indian government pages say Jupiter's sign, with the Sun's, sets the city.
beats.caption: Govt pages: Jupiter's sign + the Sun's set the city

beats.say: Haridwar, on the Ganga, needs Jupiter in Aquarius.
beats.caption: Haridwar: Jupiter in Aquarius, Sun entering Aries

beats.say: Nashik and Ujjain share Jupiter in Leo, so both are called Simhastha.
beats.caption: Nashik + Ujjain: Jupiter in Leo (Simha) → Simhastha

beats.say: We checked NASA's data: in the Indian zodiac, the last five fit.
beats.caption: NASA JPL data, Indian (sidereal) zodiac: last 5 fit

beats.say: Jupiter circles the zodiac in about twelve years. Each city waits about twelve.
beats.caption: Jupiter's lap ≈ 11.9 years → each city waits ≈ 12

beats.say: So every four years is a summary. Each city keeps Jupiter's clock.
beats.caption: “Every four years” is a summary · each city keeps Jupiter's clock
